reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-3 fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: Maria wakes up at 11:00. What time is that?
A class survey showed 3 students like costume sash and 10 students like wristband. How many students were surveyed in all?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: None of the 7 samples solves a problem involving time, days in a week, or months in a year as this lc requires: 3 are trivial clock-time restatements ('Maria wakes up at 11:00. What time is that?'), and 4 are generic word/number problems (a costume-sash survey, bare sums) with no time or calendar content whatsoever.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The lc's own vocab list is 'days in a week' and 'months in a year', but not one of the 7 samples touches either topic; every sample is either clock-time or unrelated arithmetic, leaving the entire days/months half of this competency untested.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentences stay short across all sample types, e.g. the survey word problem is 20 words, within grade-1 quarter-4 reading demand, so wording length is not the source of the alignment problem.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The costume-sash survey item (seed 44) is a plain two-addend sum dressed as a word problem but shares no connection to time at all, showing the addition DNA paired with this node is not being embedded in a time-relevant scenario as the competency needs.

competency_alignment.rationale: 'Maria wakes up at 11:00. What time is that?' restates the given time back as a question rather than posing an elapsed-time or scheduling problem (e.g. 'class starts at 9:00 and lasts an hour, when does it end?'), so even the on-topic samples fail to be a 'problem' in the sense this lc names.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: I verified the arithmetic in the off-topic samples (3+10=13, 1+15=16, 2+12=14) is all correct and the magnitudes are grade-1 appropriate, though this doesn't offset the complete absence of genuine time/day/month content.
